mutants.description: Once pgood_LED is lit, it stays lit through comparator dropouts for as long as the supervisor is in S_RUN. The designer assumed the supervisor's window trip would catch a real loss of regulation, so the LED goes dark only on leaving S_RUN instead of following the comparator.
mutants.reason: With run_active high and pgood_LED lit, a fall of pgood leaves pgood_LED lit until run_active falls. In the original it goes dark on the next clock.

mutants.description: Red_LED2 (over-temperature) stays lit after OTP clears for as long as hiccup strikes are outstanding. The 'recently troubled' persistence meant for the Red_LED1 strike blink is applied to the thermal indicator as well, instead of showing only the live OTP condition.
mutants.reason: If otp_state falls while strike_level is non-zero, Red_LED2 stays lit until strike_level returns to zero. In the original it goes dark one clock after otp_state falls.

mutants.description: The strike blink is turned off whenever Green_LED is lit, so a board that is visibly running shows only one indicator. This breaks the header rule that Green and Red_LED1 are both lit during the clean-run window.
mutants.reason: With strikes outstanding, no fault live and the converter in S_SS or S_RUN (Green_LED lit), Red_LED1 stays dark instead of blinking. If a live fault keeps Green dark in those states, the blink still shows. That second case is what separates this from the 'only while not switching' mutant.
